notes: Independently read all 39 eligible production JS/TS-family source files, package.json, openclaw.plugin.json, root/extensions/SDK instructions, local barrel provenance and relevant public SDK export/type contracts at the pinned commit. The 71-file plugin inventory partitions into 41 reviewed and 30 excluded files.

No production relative import leaves extensions/x. Local admin/channel/runtime/secret-contract/verified-GitHub/work-origin API barrels and literal lazy module descriptors remain included. They reexport plugin-owned wrappers/values rather than directly imported SDK symbols, so they do not create synthetic SDK reexport findings. Shared SDK internals and separately installed packages are outside the source boundary.

The entry descriptor names setXRuntime; src/runtime.ts uses createPluginRuntimeStore<PluginRuntime>. Thus getXRuntime handles and core/runtime aliases retain public runtime provenance. Bare api.runtime propagation is traced through local helpers without a root runtime or api.runtime identity. Pick<OpenClawPluginApi, runtime> selects the runtime handle only; it does not create a root path.

Literal Pick selections establish type references to api.on, api.registerGatewayMethod, api.logger, runtime.state.openKeyedStore, runtime.state.resolveStateDir and runtime.logging.getChildLogger. Runtime state is also independently read for reference comparison in spend.ts, so runtime.state has its own runtime member-access finding.

Plugin-owned XApiClient variables named api, channel status snapshots named runtime, admin request context, service scheduler/logger, ControlUiHost and ControlUiView contexts are distinct contracts, not OpenClawPluginApi or PluginRuntime handles. No public API/runtime paths are inferred for those objects.

Keyed store/queue/ingress monitor/secret-contract/account helper return values and child logger instances are not PluginRuntime; their calls do not extend public runtime paths or add calls to the creating SDK export. The error returned by createChannelIngressError and functions returned by createRuntimeConfigReader/createStaticReplyToModeResolver remain SDK result values, not direct unchanged export aliases.

fetch.ts destructures three direct dynamic SDK modules in Promise.all. Its authorize function passes fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher unchanged as dispatch and directly invokes it; this contributes call on that SDK export. The authorize return wrapper itself is plugin-owned. Dynamic imports narrowed by destructuring retain named-export provenance, without an unobserved namespace-star dependency.

Only manifest.channels:x is an agreed manifest contract identity. Categories, controlUi hashed build paths, package channel metadata and config/activation fields are descriptive/build metadata, not additional identities. This source audit includes the TSX UI source and erased types; it does not assert the generated published artifact has the same dependencies.

Test directory callers and the explicitly test-only test-api.ts boundary were checked. No production source imports those helpers. Reviewed production contents were individually compared with git show at the pinned commit before hashing.

Reference-kind sets were reconciled across all source occurrences; evidence is representative per kind and affected file. reviewedFiles.findingCount counts distinct findings with recorded evidence in that file, not occurrences.

Evidence reconciliation: manifest.channels:x is evidenced by the channels field and literal x value, not its closing delimiter. Multiline named imports now cite the selected symbol with module-line provenance; Promise.all dynamic imports also include their named destructuring binding.
